title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have model parameter counts far exceeding dense models of equivalent compute cost, making checkpoint-based fault tolerance extremely expensive in terms of checkpoint size, write bandwidth, and recovery time for distributed training at >10k node scale.
motivation: Distributed training clusters beyond 10k nodes have high failure rates, making fault tolerance essential, but the large parameter footprint of MoE models (many experts, sparse activation) creates checkpoint overhead disproportionate to the actual training compute.
method: MoE models only activate (use) a subset of experts (specialized sub-networks) per token, so most expert parameters never get updated in a given training step. MoC-System exploits this sparsity by saving (checkpointing) only the experts that were actually activated and updated, completely skipping the dormant ones—drastically reducing checkpoint file sizes. To manage I/O overhead, the system overlaps checkpoint writes with forward and backward computation, and spreads checkpoint data across nodes by expert grouping (expert-parallel sharding) to minimize per-node storage.
key_novelty: Instead of saving all expert parameters, the system only saves the ones actually used in each training step, which dramatically shrinks checkpoint files and reduces I/O overhead while keeping the system able to recover from failures.
contributions: Analysis of the fault tolerance bottleneck specific to sparse MoE model training at scale
MoC-System: selective expert checkpointing based on sparse activation patterns
Distributed checkpoint orchestration overlapping I/O with computation
Demonstrated reduction in checkpoint overhead while maintaining full fault recovery capability
